classificationLegend.SERIALIZED: Exact gameplay input encoded by relevant selected wire/component.
classificationLegend.FIXED_BY_EXISTING_VALIDATION: Omitted/redundant value constrained by original validation at trusted boundaries; no validation on new reads.
classificationLegend.DERIVED_FROM_AUTHENTICATED_ENCODED_STATE: Deterministically derived from encoded immutable fields and actual selected immutable policy; derivation is not automatically permitted on V1 reads.
classificationLegend.TRUSTED_PRIVATE_CAPABILITY_DERIVED_AT_VE: Private owner-bound passage/projection evidence outside Snapshot; established only at existing trusted boundaries, not reconstructed by reads.
classificationLegend.TRUSTED_CURRENT_HOST_CONTEXT_NOT_A_SAVED: Current authority/request/owner binding supplied by trusted host, never authorized by save equality.

aliasClosures.detail: Copy creates new Snapshot, clones every specifically inspected relevant outer array, and clones mutable ActorState/ObjectState/CommandReceipt elements. Scalars/strings/value times copied. Snapshot.Copy is not a general recursive serializer or validator.

Journal/Operation/ApplicationData/ImmunityData/Fear all sealed/get-only. Operations and immunity kinds constructor-copy input enumerables into read-only collections. Origin/At/Expires include exact RuleTime and Int32 phase; StructuralKey and SameAs cover policy/target/origin and all semantic operation payload fields. Valid IDs exclude separator ambiguity. Read comparison is structural, not lifecycle reconstruction.

Ledger copies/wraps Applications and Immunities. ConditionInstance/ImmunityInstance/Application/Immunity hold immutable values and immutable Fear. With/End/Advance methods construct replacements rather than mutate prior objects; invoking lifecycle methods on V1 reads is still prohibited. Legacy ConditionResolutionScope.Entry is mutable and expressly excluded from the proposed carrier.

Inspected nested collections copied/read-only, shared records sealed/get-only, replacement methods return new records. Other families named only through prior codec mapping are separately scoped and do not inherit this deep-alias conclusion.

Copy retains record references; constructors own read-only arrays. Decode reconstructs phase bindings from separately encoded data; validation checks consistency. Copy/comparison must not silently rebuild or normalize phases.

Current private checkpoint constructor stores supplied canonical array directly. All inspected callers supply fresh local trusted codec output, never public arrays. Passage stores copied receipts privately. Future writer/comparator extraction must preserve this confinement or copy at the ownership boundary.
